summary: The Arabic sʕd III etymon is integrated as Turoyo stem II, exactly as in the glossary; donor-language stem numbering must not be substituted.

Helped participants appear as direct NPs and pronominal suffixes. At 32/9 aʕ belongs to the plural article of ʕiwarnoye, not an ʕam-marked beneficiary. At 61/372 the divine actor is overtly l-marked and the recipient is -li after -le.
Optative assistance uses unprefixed Infectum, while 61/372 supplies unambiguous completed help in Preterit. The spelling msaʕadle alone at 53/187 cannot settle the actor/recipient analysis.
Existing sense 2 erlauben is supported by the already quoted 28/60. No separate sense follows from a divine helper, a needy recipient, or a modal/optative context.
At 11/65, is msaʕəd an Infectum predicate or an adjective/Part act. coordinated with ṣadəq, and does aʕməx scope over both?
Confirm contraction and plural recipient indexing in msaʕadde at MAC Interview 2/2.
At 53/187, does msaʕadle contain a recipient suffix in an Infectum clause or an actor suffix in Preterit? No new form is established from this ambiguous token.
The assigned German at 32/9 omits explicit helping; verify edition alignment before selecting it as a bilingual example.
The soil of Midyat is described as unhelpful aʕməx; this extends the supporting subject beyond human/divine helpers, but finite versus adjectival status and shared scope with ṣadəq are uncertain.
